topics.content:
CIVIC EDUCATION
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 6
THEME - DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - RESPONSIBILITIES OF MEMBERS OF A HOME (PRIMARY 4)
TOPIC - CIVIC VALUES
LEARNING AREA
- Meaning of civil values
- Examples of civic value loyalty Obedience, dedication, honesty
- Need for civic values in the society
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. explain the meaning of civic value.
2. enumerate civic values.
3. discuss the need to imbibe civic values in the society.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Textbooks
2. News paper
3. Magazines
4. Biographies, etc.
METHOD OF TEACHING - Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
- Scheme of Work
- 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
- Course Book
- All Relevant Material
- Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
MEANING OF CIVIC VALUES
Civic values are the behaviors and character traits that help a country to grow and develop. These behaviors and characters promote unity and progress, when such values are imbibed by the majority of the citizens in a country.
EXAMPLES OF CIVIC VALUES
1. Obedience
2. Loyalty
3. Dedication
4. Honesty
5. Selflessness
6. Patriotism
NEED FOR CIVIC VALUES IN THE SOCIETY
1. To promote democracy.
2. To promote human rights.
3. To promote peace and harmony.
4. To promote growth and development.
5. To promote economic development:
PRESENTATION
- To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides discussion on the meaning of civic education.
Pupil’s Activities - Contribute to discussions.
3. Leads pupils to identify at least five civic values.
4. Guides pupils to identify people in the society with good civic values.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify people with good civic values.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Nation - Meaning and Characteristics (Primary 4)
LESSON EVALUATION
Pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of civic values.
2. explain the needs for civic values in the society.
3. list five civic values.

topics.title: Meaning of a Nation: Definition of a Nation, Nations of the World and Locating Nigeria on the World Map | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 6 Civic Education
topics.content:
MEANING OF A NATION: DEFINITION OF A NATION, NATIONS OF THE WORLD AND LOCATING NIGERIA ON THE WORLD MAP
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - SECOND TERM - WEEK 6
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Characteristics of National Values: Meaning, Characteristics and Demonstration of National Values (Loyalty, Cooperation and Humility) | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 5 Civic Education
TOPIC - NIGERIA AS A NATION
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of a Nation and Nations of the World
3. Nigeria as a Nation and Locating Nigeria on the World
4. Importance of knowing the Nations of the World
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of a nation.
2. Define a nation correctly.
3. Mention at least five nations of the world.
4. Identify Nigeria as a nation.
5. Locate Nigeria on the map of Africa and the world map.
6. State the importance of knowing different nations of the world.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the importance of national values and the need to be good citizens.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the meaning of a nation, examples of nations of the world, and the location of Nigeria on the world map.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. World map
2. Map of Africa
3. Globe
4. Nigerian National Flag
5. Flashcards showing the names of different countries
6. Pictures of national flags
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
People live in different countries around the world. Each country has its own name, government, flag, national anthem, and citizens. Such a country is called a nation. Nigeria is one of the many nations in the world and is located in West Africa.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of a nation, examples of nations of the world, and how to locate Nigeria on the map of Africa and the world map.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF A NATION
A nation is a group of people who live together in a particular country and are united by common laws, government, history, culture, or language.
A nation is also a country with its own government and citizens.
NATIONS OF THE WORLD
A nation is an independent country where people live under one government and share common values, rules, and national identity.
There are many nations in the world. Some examples are:
- Nigeria
- Ghana
- Kenya
- South Africa
- United Kingdom
- United States of America
- Canada
- Brazil
- China
- India
Each nation has its own:
- National Flag
- National Anthem
- Government
- Capital City
- Citizens
LESSON 2 - NIGERIA AS A NATION
Nigeria is a nation located in West Africa.
- Capital City: Abuja
- Largest City: Lagos
- National Flag: Green-White-Green
- Continent: Africa
- Citizens: Nigerians
LOCATING NIGERIA ON THE WORLD MAP
Nigeria can be found:
- On the continent of Africa.
- In the western part of Africa.
- Along the Gulf of Guinea.
- Between the countries of Benin, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF KNOWING NATIONS OF THE WORLD
Knowing different nations helps us to:
1. Understand the world better.
2. Respect people from other countries.
3. Promote peace and friendship.
4. Improve our knowledge of geography.
5. Appreciate Nigeria’s place in the world.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. A nation is ______.
A. a market with its own government
B. a classroom with its own government
C. an independent country with its own government
D. a village with its own government
2. Nigeria is located in ______.
A. West Africa
B. North America
C. Europe
D. Asia
3. Which of these is a nation?
A. Classroom
B. Lagos
C. Ghana
D. Street
4. The capital city of Nigeria is ______.
A. Lagos
B. Abuja
C. Kano
D. Ibadan
5. Nigerians are the ______ of Nigeria.
A. citizens
B. teachers
C. visitors
D. tourists
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: government, Nation, Africa, Nigeria, citizens
6. A ______ is an independent country.
7. ______ is our country.
8. Nigeria is located in ______.
9. The people of a country are called ______.
10. Every nation has its own ______.
C. True or False
11. Nigeria is a nation. ______
12. Lagos is the capital city of Nigeria. ______
13. Nigeria is located in Europe. ______
14. Every nation has its own government. ______
15. Ghana is one of the nations in asia. ______
D. Matching
16. Nigeria - A. Citizens of Nigeria
17. Abuja - B. West Africa
18. Africa - C. Capital city of Nigeria
19. Nigerians - D. Continent
20. Nation - E. Independent country
ANSWER KEYS
1. C 2. A 3. C 4. B 5. A
6. nation
7. Nigeria
8. Africa
9. citizens
10. government
11. True
12. False
13. False
14. False
15. True
16. B - West Africa
17. C - Capital city of Nigeria
18. D - Continent
19. A - Citizens of Nigeria
20. E - Independent country
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that a nation is an independent country with its own government, citizens, laws, and national identity. They identified examples of nations of the world such as Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, the United States, China, and India.
Pupils also learned that Nigeria is a nation located in West Africa, with Abuja as its capital city. They practised locating Nigeria on the map of Africa and the world map and discussed the importance of knowing different nations of the world.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays a world map, a map of Africa, a globe, and the Nigerian National Flag.
The teacher asks:
- What is the name of our country?
- On which continent is Nigeria located?
- Can you mention another country you know?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the maps and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of a Nation
The teacher explains that a nation is an independent country with its own government, citizens, laws, and national identity.
The teacher gives examples such as Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of a nation in their own words.
Step 3: Nations of the World
The teacher introduces some nations of the world:
- Nigeria
- Ghana
- Kenya
- South Africa
- United States of America
- Canada
- China
- India
- Brazil
- United Kingdom
The teacher explains that every nation has its own flag, government, capital city, and citizens.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention other countries they know.
Step 4: Locating Nigeria on the World Map
The teacher uses the world map, map of Africa, and globe to show the location of Nigeria.
The teacher explains that:
- Nigeria is in West Africa.
- Abuja is the capital city of Nigeria.
- Nigerians are the citizens of Nigeria.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify Nigeria on the map and globe.
Step 5: Importance of Knowing Nations of the World
The teacher explains that knowing different nations helps us to:
- Understand the world better.
- Respect people from other countries.
- Promote peace and friendship.
- Improve our knowledge of geography.
- Appreciate Nigeria’s place in the world.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state why it is important to know different nations.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of a nation.
- Group 2: List five nations of the world.
- Group 3: Locate Nigeria on the map of Africa and the world map.
- Group 4: State the importance of knowing different nations of the world.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of a nation, examples of nations of the world, Nigeria’s location on the world map, and the importance of knowing different nations.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice Questions, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching exercises.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Primary 4 - Civic Education Second Term - Mid Term Test Questions and Answers
Characteristics of a Nation: Common Territory, Customs, Traditions and Common Language | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 8 Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of a nation.
2. Define a nation correctly.
3. Mention at least five nations of the world.
4. Identify Nigeria as a nation.
5. Locate Nigeria on the map of Africa and the world map.
6. State the importance of knowing different nations of the world.

topics.title: Reasons Why We Should Build Our Nation: Importance, Benefits and Need for Nation Building | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 9 Civic Education
topics.content:
REAOSNS WHY WE SHOULD BUILD OUR NATION: IMPORTANCE, BENEFITS AND NEED FOR NATION BUILDING
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - SECOND TERM - WEEK 9
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Characteristics of a Nation: Common Territory, Customs, Traditions and Common Language | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 8 Civic Education
TOPIC - REASONS WHY WE SHOULD BUILD OUR NATION
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning Benefits and Importance of Nation Building
3. Reaosns why we should Build our Nation
4. Ways Pupils can help to Build the Nation
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of nation building.
2. State at least five reasons why we should build our nation.
3. Mention at least five importance of nation building.
4. State at least five benefits of nation building.
5. Identify ways pupils can contribute to nation building.
6. Demonstrate attitudes that promote national development.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned the meaning of a nation and the characteristics of a nation, including common territory, customs, traditions, and common language.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by explaining why nation building is necessary, its importance, benefits, and how every citizen, including pupils, can contribute to national development.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Nigerian National Flag
2. Pictures showing community development activities
3. Charts on nation building
5. Flashcards with the words Peace, Unity, Development, Patriotism, Responsibility
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every citizen has a role to play in making Nigeria a better country. When people obey the law, respect one another, work hard, keep the environment clean, and protect public property, they help to build the nation. This is called nation building.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of nation building, the reasons why we should build our nation, the importance and benefits of nation building, and how they can contribute to the development of Nigeria through good behaviour and responsible citizenship.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF NATION BUILDING
Nation building is the process of working together to make a country peaceful, united, safe, and developed.
Nation building involves citizens and leaders contributing to the progress of their country.
REASONS WHY WE SHOULD BUILD OUR NATION
We should build our nation because it helps to:
1. Promote peace and unity.
2. Develop the country.
3. Create a safe environment.
4. Improve education and healthcare.
5. Protect public property.
6. Reduce poverty and unemployment.
7. Encourage responsible citizenship.
8. Make the country respected by other nations.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF NATION BUILDING
Nation building is important because it:
1. Encourages national unity.
2. Promotes peaceful coexistence.
3. Helps citizens work together.
4. Improves the economy.
5. Encourages patriotism.
6. Builds good leadership.
7. Strengthens national development.
BENEFITS OF NATION BUILDING
The benefits of nation building include:
1. Better roads and public facilities.
2. Good schools and hospitals.
3. More employment opportunities.
4. Peaceful communities.
5. National progress and development.
6. Improved standard of living.
7. Stronger relationship among citizens.
LESSON 3 - WAYS PUPILS CAN HELP BUILD THE NATION
Pupils can help by:
1. Obeying school rules.
2. Respecting parents, teachers, and elders.
3. Keeping the environment clean.
4. Protecting public property.
5. Being honest and hardworking.
6. Living peacefully with others.
7. Participating in community activities.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Nation building means ______.
A. destroying public property
B. working together to develop the country
C. fighting with one another
D. breaking the law
2. Which of these is a reason for nation building?
A. To break school rules
B. To encourage violence
C. To waste public money
D. To promote peace and unity
3. One benefit of nation building is ______.
A. more quarrels
B. more crime
C. better roads and schools
D. poor leadership
4. Which of these helps to build the nation?
A. Damaging public property
B. Keeping the environment clean
C. Refusing to obey rules
D. Telling lies
5. Good citizens build the nation through ______.
A. honesty and hard work
B. laziness
C. corruption
D. violence
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: peace, unity, development, honest, nation
6. Nation building promotes ______.
7. We should work together to build our ______.
8. Honesty and hard work encourage national ______.
9. Good citizens should be ______.
10. Nation building promotes ______ among citizens.
C. True or False
11. Nation building helps to develop a country. ______
12. Protecting public property is not part of nation building. ______
13. Fighting promotes nation building. ______
14. Every citizen has a role in nation building. ______
15. Keeping the environment clean helps to build the nation. ______
D. Matching
16. Nation building - A. National progress
17. Peace - B. Working together
18. Development - C. Living without fighting
19. Unity - D. Growth of the country
20. Cooperation - E. People working as one
ANSWER KEYS
1. B 2. D 3. C 4. B 5. A
6. peace
7. nation
8. development
9. honest
10. unity
11. True
12. False
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. B - Working together
17. C - Living without fighting
18. D - Growth of the country
19. E - People working as one
20. A - National progress
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned the meaning of nation building and understood that it is the process of working together to make the country peaceful, united, safe, and developed. They discussed the reasons why we should build our nation, including promoting peace, unity, security, and national development.
Pupils also learned the importance and benefits of nation building, such as improving education, healthcare, roads, employment opportunities, and the standard of living.
They identified ways they can contribute to nation building by obeying rules, respecting others, protecting public property, keeping the environment clean, and being honest and hardworking.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of people cleaning the environment, planting trees, obeying traffic rules, repairing roads, and helping one another.
The teacher asks:
- What are the people doing?
- How do these activities help our country?
- Who should help to build Nigeria?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Nation Building
The teacher explains that nation building means working together to make the country peaceful, united, safe, and developed. Also, the teacher explains that both leaders and citizens have important roles to play in nation building.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of nation building in their own words.
Step 3: Reasons Why We Should Build Our Nation
The teacher explains that nation building is necessary because it:
- Promotes peace and unity.
- Develops the country.
- Creates a safe environment.
- Improves education and healthcare.
- Encourages responsible citizenship.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention reasons why nation building is important.
Step 4: Importance and Benefits of Nation Building
The teacher explains that nation building:
- Encourages cooperation.
- Improves roads, schools, and hospitals.
- Creates employment opportunities.
- Promotes good leadership.
- Improves the standard of living.
- Makes the country respected by other nations.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the importance and benefits of nation building.
Step 5: Ways Pupils Can Help Build the Nation
The teacher explains that pupils can contribute to nation building by:
- Obeying school rules.
- Respecting parents, teachers, and elders.
- Keeping the environment clean.
- Protecting public property.
- Being honest and hardworking.
- Living peacefully with others.
- Participating in community activities.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss ways they can help build Nigeria.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of nation building.
- Group 2: State reasons why we should build our nation.
- Group 3: Mention the importance and benefits of nation building.
- Group 4: Explain how pupils can contribute to nation building.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of nation building, the reasons for nation building, the importance and benefits of nation building, and the roles pupils can play in national development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice Questions, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching exercises.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Duties and Responsibilities of Parents and Children in Building the Nation | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 10 Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of nation building.
2. State at least five reasons why we should build our nation.
3. Mention at least five importance of nation building.
4. State at least five benefits of nation building.
5. Identify ways pupils can contribute to nation building.
6. Demonstrate attitudes that promote national development.

topics.title: Duties and Responsibilities of Parents and Children in Building the Nation | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 10 Civic Education
topics.content:
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF PARENTS AND CHILDREN IN BUILDING THE NATION
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 10
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Reasons Why We Should Build Our Nation: Importance, Benefits and Need for Nation Building | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 9 Civic Education
TOPIC - DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF PARENTS AND CHILDREN IN BUILDING THE NATION
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Duties and Responsibilities
3. Duties and Responsibilities of Parents and Children
4. Impottance of Parents and Children Duties and Responsibilities
5. Ways Parents and Children can help to Build the Nation
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of duties and responsibilities.
2. Mention at least five duties and responsibilities of parents.
3. Mention at least five duties and responsibilities of children.
4. State the importance of parents and children performing their responsibilities.
5. Identify ways parents and children can contribute to nation building.
6. Demonstrate responsible behaviour at home, in school, and in the community.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about nation building, its importance, benefits, and the roles citizens play in developing the nation.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by explaining the duties and responsibilities of parents and children in building a peaceful and progressive nation.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts showing parents caring for children
2. Pictures of children helping with household chores
3. Flashcards with the words Duty and Responsibility
4. Pictures showing children studying, cleaning, and obeying parents
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every family has responsibilities that help the home, community, and country grow. Parents have the duty to care for and guide their children, while children also have responsibilities such as obeying their parents, studying hard, and helping at home. When both parents and children perform their responsibilities, they help to build a peaceful, responsible, and developed nation.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the duties and responsibilities of parents and children, their importance, and how these responsibilities contribute to nation building.
MEANING OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Duties are tasks or jobs that a person is expected to do.
Responsibilities are obligations or things a person is expected to do carefully for the good of others and society.
Both parents and children have important duties that help to build the nation.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF PARENTS
Parents should:
1. Provide food, clothing, and shelter for their children.
2. Send their children to school.
3. Teach good morals and discipline.
4. Protect and care for their children.
5. Encourage honesty and hard work.
6. Pay school fees when necessary.
7. Guide children to become responsible citizens.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF CHILDREN
Children should:
1. Respect and obey their parents.
2. Attend school regularly.
3. Study hard and complete assignments.
4. Help with household chores.
5. Respect teachers, elders, and other people.
6. Keep the home and school environment clean.
7. Protect public property.
8. Be honest, disciplined, and hardworking.
IMPORTANCE OF PARENTS AND CHILDREN’S RESPONSIBILITIES
When parents and children perform their responsibilities:
1. Families become peaceful.
2. Children grow into responsible adults.
3. Society becomes safer.
4. National development is promoted.
5. Good values are passed to future generations.
6. Peace, unity, and cooperation are encouraged.
WAYS PARENTS AND CHILDREN CAN HELP BUILD THE NATION
1. Obey the law.
2. Respect one another.
3. Work hard.
4. Keep the environment clean.
5. Protect public property.
6. Show honesty and patriotism.
7. Cooperate with others.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. A duty is ______.
A. a task a person is expected to do
B. a game people play
C. a type of food
D. a festival
2. One responsibility of parents is to ______.
A. tell lies
B. send their children to school
C. destroy public property
D. refuse to care for their children
3. One responsibility of children is to ______.
A. obey their parents
B. fight their classmates
C. skip school
D. damage school property
4. Which of these helps in nation building?
A. Laziness and sluggish
B. Honesty and hard work
C. Violence and fighting
D. Theft and robbery
5. Parents and children should work together to ______.
A. encourage corruption
B. break the law
C. build the nation
D. destroy the environment
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: children, responsibility, school, parents, respect
6. ______ should care for their children.
7. ______ should obey their parents.
8. Every child should attend ______ regularly.
9. We should show ______ to parents, teachers, and elders.
10. Performing your ______ helps to build the nation.
C. True or False
11. Parents should provide food, clothing, and shelter for their children. ______
12. Children should respect and obey their parents. ______
13. Helping with household chores is one responsibility of children. ______
14. Nation building is the duty of only the government. ______
15. Good families help to build a better nation. ______
D. Matching
16. Parents - A. Respect and obedience
17. Children - B. Attend school
18. Teacher - C. Cares for the family
19. Pupil - D. Teaches pupils
20. Family - E. Foundation of the nation
ANSWER KEYS
1. A 2. B 3. A 4. C 5. D
6. parents
7. children
8. school
9. respect
10. responsibility
11. True
12. True
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. C - Cares for the family
17. A - Respect and obedience
18. D - Teaches pupils
19. B - Attend school
20. E - Foundation of the nation
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned the meaning of duties and responsibilities and identified the different duties of parents and children. They learned that parents are responsible for providing food, clothing, shelter, education, guidance, and care for their children, while children are expected to obey their parents, respect elders, attend school regularly, study hard, and help with household chores.
Pupils also learned that when parents and children perform their responsibilities faithfully, they help to build peaceful families, responsible citizens, and a better nation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of parents caring for their children, children helping with household chores, pupils studying in class, and families working together.
The teacher asks:
- What are the parents doing?
- What are the children doing?
- Why should every member of the family perform his or her duties?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Duties and Responsibilities
The teacher explains that:
- Duties are tasks or jobs a person is expected to do.
- Responsibilities are obligations a person should perform carefully for the good of others and society.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meanings of duties and responsibilities in their own words.
Step 3: Duties and Responsibilities of Parents
The teacher explains that parents should:
- Provide food, clothing, and shelter.
- Send their children to school.
- Teach good morals and discipline.
- Protect and care for their children.
- Guide their children to become responsible citizens.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention other responsibilities of parents.
Step 4: Duties and Responsibilities of Children
The teacher explains that children should:
- Obey and respect their parents.
- Attend school regularly.
- Study hard.
- Help with household chores.
- Respect teachers and elders.
- Keep their environment clean.
- Protect public property.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss how they carry out their responsibilities at home and in school.
Step 5: Importance of Performing Responsibilities
The teacher explains that when parents and children perform their responsibilities:
- Families become peaceful.
- Children grow into responsible adults.
- Society develops.
- Peace and unity are promoted.
- Nation building becomes easier.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the importance of performing their responsibilities.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: List the duties of parents.
- Group 2: List the duties of children.
- Group 3: Explain why parents and children should perform their responsibilities.
- Group 4: State ways parents and children can help build the nation.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of duties and responsibilities, the duties of parents, the duties of children, and their importance in nation building.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice Questions, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching exercises.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
